title: Affine perfect replacement with a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], with derived localizations for its module category and each localized open site [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $D$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], strictly zero above a natural degree $d$, whose terms are quasi-coherent. Suppose its derived image is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then there exist a complex $C$, an integer $a$, a natural $b$, and a quasi-isomorphism $e:C\to D$ such that $C$ is strictly zero outside $[a,b]$ and every term is quasi-coherent, finitely presented and flat over the identity of $Y$ [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. No comparison with higher direct images is asserted.

proof.text: Identify the affine scheme with the spectrum of its global sections. The quasi-coherent complex D corresponds to its complex of sections under the affine derived equivalence. Perfectness supplies a bounded finite-projective ring representative.

A bounded projective complex is K-projective. Represent its derived isomorphism to the section complex by a chain map using bijectivity on homotopy morphisms; invertibility of its derived image implies that this map is a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply exact associated sheaves termwise, transport back along the affine chart, and compose with the quasi-coherent counit to D. Bounds transfer termwise. Finite-projective modules are direct summands of finite free modules, so their associated sheaves are flat, quasi-coherent and finitely presented. Enlarge the upper integer bound to a natural number. For empty Y or zero D the zero complex suffices.
